evidence.description: A DateFormatter is instantiated inside the computed property 'localizedMonthAndYear' every time the property is accessed.
A DateFormatter is instantiated inside the 'fetchAndUpdate' method every time the function is called.

candidates.explanation: DateFormatter is an expensive object to initialize. Creating new instances within property getters or frequently called methods instead of reusing a static or cached instance is a performance anti-pattern.
candidates.title: Inefficient DateFormatter instantiation

evidence.description: The code uses 'as? [String: Any]' to cast the result of JSONSerialization, which can lead to issues if the JSON structure deviates from expectations.
The code uses 'as? [String: Any]' to cast the object associated with the latest key.

candidates.explanation: Relying on 'Any' dictionaries for JSON parsing bypasses the type safety provided by Swift's Decodable protocol, making the code more prone to runtime errors and harder to maintain.
candidates.title: Force casting and type safety concerns

evidence.description: The code first uses JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with:) to parse data into a dictionary, then later uses JSONSerialization.data(withJSONObject:) to convert a subset of that dictionary back into Data to decode it into a Report struct.

candidates.explanation: Converting Data to a Dictionary and then back to Data to use JSONDecoder is inefficient. The code should ideally decode the desired object directly from the initial Data buffer.
candidates.title: Redundant JSON Serialization
